claims.text: Nickel-based superalloys exhibit enhanced temperature-dependent plastic deformation behavior.
The enhanced deformation behavior is caused by the high-temperature evolution of γ' precipitates.
Evolution of γ' precipitates improves creep resistance.
Evolution of γ' precipitates facilitates dynamic recrystallization.
The initial nickel-based superalloy has a stable ambient-temperature distribution of γ' precipitates.
Elevated temperature under mechanical stress causes growth, coarsening, or redistribution of γ' precipitates.
High-temperature microstructural changes in γ' precipitates enhance dynamic recrystallization.
High-temperature microstructural changes in γ' precipitates alter dislocation mobility.
Enhanced dynamic recrystallization and altered dislocation mobility collectively improve creep resistance.
Enhanced dynamic recrystallization and altered dislocation mobility modify plastic deformation behavior.
At elevated temperature, the material will have greater creep resistance than under ambient-temperature baseline conditions.
At elevated temperature, the material will have a higher dynamic recrystallization rate than under ambient-temperature baseline conditions.
Under ambient or low-temperature conditions, the superalloy exhibits less dynamic plastic deformation and minimal precipitate-structure change.
The proposed behavior is limited to nickel-based superalloys having a well-defined γ' phase and may not extend to alloy systems without comparable precipitate stabilizers.
